name: Phact
description: A star 80 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: radius 10.435 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 411.675 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.874) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: effective temperature 8054 +/- 3803 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.31)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: distance 80.128 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.029), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 80 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 412 times the Sun's luminosity at 8,054 K, so 10.435 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 26634: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Columbae
quotes.card: Alpha Columbae is a third magnitude star in the southern constellation of Columba.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Phact ; Alpha Columbae is the Bayer designation, which is Latinized from α Columbae.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2900546759663847168 (quality C), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
